newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila SEC to submit findings on insider trading.
newsitem.headline: Manila SEC to submit findings on insider trading.

text.p: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chairman Perfecto Yasay told Reuters on Friday he would submit to the Congress a list of firms and brokers allegedly involved in insider trading.
"We will submit a list of the cases being investigated by the Philippine Stock Exchange... We are not at liberty to disclose the details." Yasay told Reuters in an interview.
The list would be submitted to the House Committee on Banks and Financial Intermediaries, he said.
The list compiled by the Philippine Stock Exchange followed investigations begun in 1995, he said.
Yasay said there were 30 to 50 firms mentioned on the list but he declined to give details.
He did not say when the list would be submitted to the Congress but said it would be as soon as possible.
Yasay said of the entire list, some were still being investigated by the Philippine Stock Exchange while other cases had been completed.
The Philippine bourse was rocked last week by a series of resignations by senior officials, including the president Vitaliano Nanagas.
Members of the bourse's governing board said Nanagas had to leave because his management style had angered the staff.
Nanagas had brought in his own team of people at very high salaries, they said.
Nanagas said his aim was to professionalise the bourse and said that he "may have moved too fast."
Market speculation was that there was intense rivaly within the bourse on implementing a series of tough reform measures aimed at making the bourse transparent.
Insider trading is a crime under the Revised Securities Act passed in 1981.
SEC officials said so far no one in the Philippines had been prosecuted for insider trading.
